title: Compact CI bootloader and incremental dependency pruner
author: Samir Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces a compact CI bootloader that centralizes environment setup and a dependency pruner stage. Reduces cold presubmit time by ~30% and removes stale devdeps from the build path. No runtime or API changes.
description: Motivation: Our presubmit setup and integration pipelines have become a major contributor to CI queue time and flaky installs. Multiple repos repeat the same environment boot steps (toolchain setup, auth, environment variables) and we carry transitive devdeps that rarely change. This PR introduces a compact CI bootloader (a small Go entrypoint) to centralize common bootstrapping and an incremental dependency pruner stage that proactively removes unused dev dependencies before the heavy install phase. Goals: 1) Reduce presubmit setup latency, 2) Make pipeline steps idempotent and cache-friendly, 3) Surface dependency churn to the dev workflow via a curated bot. What we changed: - Add cmd/ci-bootloader (Go) that runs early in all presubmit lanes; it performs hermetic toolchain checks, runtime selection, and populates a slim layer for subsequent steps. - Introduce .github/actions/dep-pruner composite action that inspects package manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod) and produces a minimal package set to install; it can run in dry-run mode and emits structured annotations for the CLI and Console. - Split the heavy integration test lanes into runtime-aware shards (node, python, go) and wire them to new lightweight Docker microimages (ci-slim-node, ci-slim-python) to keep cache layers shallow. - Integrate with the dep-curator bot (backend service) to propose pruning PRs when unused devdeps are detected across the monorepo. - Update top-level CI templates (workflows/presubmit.yml) to invoke ci-bootloader and dep-pruner early and to adopt the new test shard matrix. Backwards compatibility: All existing job outputs are preserved. The bootloader uses a feature-flag (CI_BOOTLOADER=enabled) so we can roll back to legacy behavior in runway. Checklist: - [x] Add ci-bootloader command and unit tests - [x] Implement dep-pruner action and dry-run annotations - [x] Create new slim test images and adjust buildx cache keys - [x] Integrate dep-curator hook and documentation - [x] Update docs and quickstart for contributors - [x] Run full monorepo presubmit suite on ephemeral runners (two successful runs) Commits (summary): - feat(ci): add ci-bootloader Go entrypoint and unit tests - feat(ci): add dep-pruner composite action (node + python handlers) - feat(ci): add slim ci images and runtime-aware test sharding - chore(ci): update presubmit templates and makefile targets - ci: wire dep-curator webhook and dry-run annotations Changed areas / representative files (high level): - cmd/ci-bootloader/main.go - .github/actions/dep-pruner/action.yml - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml - images/ci-slim-node/Dockerfile - images/ci-slim-python/Dockerfile - tools/dep-curator/README.md - Makefile (targets: ci-boot, dep-prune) - scripts/ci/compare-cache-key.sh Small illustrative snippet (ci-bootloader env selection): "if runtime == 'node' && hasNodeToolchain() { setToolchain('node', '18.x') } else { fallbackTo('docker:node:18-slim') }" Review notes and discussion: Reviewer Aisha: "Nice centralization — please ensure the bootloader exits nonzero only for fatal infra problems. Nonfatal warnings should annotate and continue to avoid breaking flaky runners." Author reply (Samir): "Agreed. Bootloader now emits WARN vs ERROR annotations; nonfatal checks return 0 with a 'warn' annotation. Fatal checks set CI_BROKEN=1 and exit 2." Reviewer Diego: "Dep-pruner looks promising. A few comments: i) add a strict whitelist for top-level scripts, ii) ensure yarn.lock integrity check runs in dry-run mode to avoid drift." Author reply: "Added whitelist and an integrity check mode (-i) that compares lockfile hashes and reports annotations instead of modifying files in dry-run." Reviewer Morgan: "Are the new slim images compatible with our flaky integration tests that rely on system packages?" Author reply: "We kept an escape hatch: TEST_IMAGE=legacy will use the fuller image. Also added a smoke job that runs the legacy image weekly to catch regressions." CI checks and history: - Initial push (5 commits): lint failed on the repo-wide shellcheck due to a renamed script; fixed in follow-up commit. - Second run: one flaky test in python shard (test_integration_db) failed intermittently; reran the job and it passed. - Final run: all checks passed: unit (go/node/python) ✓, lint ✓, smoke-integration shards ✓, presubmit matrix ✓. Observability: Added metrics emitted by ci-bootloader: boot_time_ms, cache_hit_ratio, pruner_recommendations_count. These are scraped by the CI telemetry pipeline for rollout monitoring. Dep-curator flow: When the pruner detects >3 stale devdeps in a package, it will open a draft PR with a suggested package.json/pyproject patch, list the tests that exercise the package (heuristic), and include a confidence score. The bot respects OWNER files and will not propose changes for packages in the vendor/ or third_party/ directories. Rollout plan: - Week 0 (canary): Enable CI_BOOTLOADER only on fastpath lanes for 5 engineering teams. - Week 1: Expand to main presubmit lanes and enable dry-run pruner annotations for all repos. - Week 2: Turn on automatic draft PR creation for low-risk targets and monitor telemetry. Merge strategy and outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-28 after green CI and approvals from Aisha and Diego. No post-merge release required for customers. Follow-ups: - ENG-2133: extend pruner to detect unused transitive devdeps (prototype) - ENG-2140: expose boot metrics in Console dashboard - ENG-2152: add Windows-compatible slim images (WIP)
